subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should OpenClaw publish a corrected stable hotfix for the affected `2026.6.11` package now, promote a fixed beta, or leave users on the current stable until the next normal stable release?
rationale: The source-side fix is already merged and the beta package appears to include corrected dist plumbing, but `npm latest` and GitHub latest stable still point to the broken `2026.6.11` artifact; release publication and stable channel policy require maintainer intent.

options.title: Publish a stable hotfix
options.body: Cut a corrected stable package from the fixed source and verify npm tarball parity plus an installed gateway smoke before closing this issue.

options.title: Point users to beta until next stable
options.body: Keep this issue open but document the beta workaround and wait for the next stable train to carry the fix.

options.title: Wait for the next scheduled stable silently
options.body: Accept that stable `latest` users remain exposed until the next normal stable release, with no hotfix or explicit workaround.

recommendation.title: Publish a stable hotfix
recommendation.body: Cut a corrected stable package from the fixed source and verify npm tarball parity plus an installed gateway smoke before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is release/package handling, and Vincent Koc is tied to the latest stable release commit and recent current-main release/debug work in the inspected history.
